rubrics.justification: The response gives a broad blastocyst description but overstates certainty and assigns a very high-grade range (4AA/4AB/5AA/5AB) without image-grounded specificity; it fabricates details like uniform TE and tightly packed ICM rather than carefully limiting claims to visible features.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age-related aneuploidy risk, ovarian reserve, prior live birth, PCOS, sperm motility, and endometrium, though some links to embryo competence are somewhat overstated.

The reasoning is generally structured and internally consistent, but it overweights prior live birth and morphology while underappreciating age-related euploidy limits, leading to an optimistic implantation estimate.

Recommendations such as SET for a good-quality day-5 blastocyst and consideration of PGT-A at age 38 are broadly guideline-consistent, though the prognosis framing is somewhat more confident than evidence typically supports.

It provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, monitoring, cryopreservation, and future-cycle discussion, but lacks more nuanced contingency planning and specifics around counseling on age-related miscarriage/aneuploidy risk.
